"You are an expert game developer. Recreate the 2007 Digital Chocolate Java ME game \"Kamikaze Robots\" as accurately as possible as a modern desktop/web game.

TECH STACK
- Prefer Godot 4 (GDScript) or HTML5 Canvas + TypeScript/Phaser, or pure Java with LibGDX if you prefer. Choose one and stick to it. Make it immediately playable (desktop window or browser).
- Keep the original low-res, cute, cartoon mobile aesthetic (pixel-art or simple vector with chunky outlines). Target \~320×480 or 480×320 portrait/landscape side-view.

CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP (must match original feel)
1. Race starts with the player robot perched at the top of a jagged/bumpy downhill slope. A large mechanical foot animates and kicks it.
2. While airborne the robot automatically spins clockwise at a rate influenced by the Spin stat.
3. Single-button control: hold the button (or hold mouse/touch) to reverse/brake the spin and orient the feet downward. Release to spin freely. Timing is everything.
4. Physics:
   - More free spin before landing = higher speed and longer/more powerful bounce.
   - Landing cleanly on both feet = strong upward/forward bounce and minimal damage.
   - Landing on one foot, arms, body, or head = reduced bounce + damage.
5. Damage system (critical):
   - Limbs detach progressively: arms first, then legs.
   - Visual: parts fly off with physics and can bounce around.
   - When only torso + head remain, the next impact can eject the head forward with an explosion trail (distance controlled by Explosion stat). If the head crosses the finish line you still win.
   - If the robot fully explodes before the finish, the race is lost.
6. Camera follows the robot smoothly. Show distance traveled (meters) at the top like the original.
7. AI opponents (1–3) race the same course. They appear as full robots or distinct shadows. They never fall apart as badly as the player.

PROGRESSION @COMMENT_BODY@ CHIPS
- Tournament mode with 25–30 levels of increasing length, steepness, and obstacle density (bumps, gaps, steeper sections).
- After every race award up to 4 chips:
  - Finish 1st
  - Achieve a required number of spins in a single jump
  - Reach a minimum jump height
  - Cover a certain distance
- Between races open an upgrade screen. Spend chips on four stats (each level has visible effect):
  - Jump (bounce height/power)
  - Spin (base rotation speed)
  - Stamina (damage resistance / how many bad landings before limbs fall)
  - Explosion (head launch distance and speed)
- Allow replaying any previously cleared level to farm missing chips.
- Optional: cosmetic body upgrades at chip thresholds (different robot skins).

MODES
- Tournament (main progression).
- Quick Race / Practice (any unlocked level, vs AI or solo).
- Simple local multiplayer (pass-and-play: up to 3 humans take turns, or simultaneous if easy).

VISUAL @COMMENT_BODY@ AUDIO STYLE
- Cute round robots with big expressive eyes, spring-loaded feet, and detachable limbs.
- Colorful cartoon hills, some levels with space/planet backgrounds matching classic screenshots.
- Particles for sparks, limb detachment, and the flaming head comet.
- Upbeat, silly chiptune/MIDI-style music and punchy SFX (kick, bounce, metal hit, explosion).

UI
- Distance meter at top.
- Chip progress indicators during race.
- Clean upgrade screen with four bars/sliders.
- Simple menu: Tournament, Quick Race, Upgrades, Settings.

IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
- Deliver a complete, runnable project with clear instructions how to build/run.
- Make physics feel snappy and readable (original was praised for good physics).
- Include at least 8–10 hand-crafted levels of rising difficulty (procedural is fine as bonus later).
- Add a short “How to Play” screen that explains the one-button spin control and limb loss.
- Keep the code clean, commented, and modular so levels and stats are easy to tweak.
- Target 60 FPS, responsive controls, and satisfying bounce feedback.

Start by scaffolding the project, implementing the core robot physics + one-button spin control + limb destruction, then a single complete level with AI, then the chip/upgrade system, then more levels and menus.

Make the recreation as faithful as possible to the 2007 original’s feel, humor, and destruction loop.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.

Empty repo with build scripts. Let me check the default-start script to understand how the project is served/run.

The runtime supports a Vite project or a plain index.html. I'll build an HTML5 Canvas + TypeScript game with Vite. That's a good fit. Need to be playable, deterministic, and visually faithful.

Let me plan the game architecture:

- Vite + TypeScript, no heavy dependencies. Canvas 2D rendering, custom physics. Portrait 480x720? Original mobile was 320x480 portrait. The prompt asks ~320x480 or 480x320. I'll do 480x800-ish scaled canvas with letterboxing, or 480x720? Let's target a logical resolution 480x720 portrait to match 2007 mobile. Actually 320x480 was classic. Target logical 360x640 with pixel-art scaling? For desktop, a 480x720 canvas centered, scaled up to fit window with crisp scaling disabled? Hand-drawn vector with chunky outlines looks good at high DPI.

Design: full-screen canvas, internal resolution 480x720 (portrait), scale to fit window. Draw simple vector cartoon shapes with chunky dark outlines, gradients, parallax hills, stars for space levels.

Core mechanics:
- Terrain: jagged downhill slope defined by an array of segments/columns. Use a heightfield from x=0 to level length; generated from hand-crafted level configs (seed, length, slope, bumpiness, gaps).
- Physics: robot as a point with radius, rotating body. On ground contact, compute local contact points (feet vs arms vs head). Simpler: robot has spin angle; feet are at angle pointing "down" of the robot sprite. At bounce, determine orientation factor = how close feet are to below (cos of angle difference). Resolve landing based on angle bands: both feet (|a| < 12°), one foot (12-35°), side/arm (35-70°), body (70-110°), head (>110°).
- The robot bounces: jump power = baseJump * landingQuality * (1 + freeSpin * spinBonus) — more spin before landing increases speed/bounce but makes clean landing harder. Need a risk/reward: free-spin count increases power multiplier. Actually original: hold to brake spin; you want to release at right time so feet are down when landing; more free spin = higher speed. Implement: track rotation while airborne; spinCharge = number of full rotations performed; land power multiplier = 1 + min(spins, 6)*0.12. Clean-feet landing gives high bounce (vertical + forward), bad landing gives low bounce and damage.
- Damage: stamina determines hits; limbs (left arm, right arm, left leg, right leg) detach on bad landings progressively: arms first, then legs. Each bad landing consumes 1 stamina point and detaches a limb (arms first). When no limbs and another bad landing: head ejects with explosion trail; head becomes projectile with velocity, can still cross finish line to win. If head explodes/stops before finish → lose. Actually "If the robot fully explodes before the finish, the race is lost." Head state = final chance. Head keeps bouncing forward with explosion particles, distance controlled by Explosion stat; after head loses momentum, race lost. If head crosses finish, win.

- Limbs fly off with physics, bounce on terrain, drawn behind.

- Camera follows robot smoothly, distance meter at top in meters. Finish line at level length.

- Spin control: hold mouse/space to brake spin (slow spin rate to near zero) and maybe slightly rotate toward feet-down? Original says "hold the button to reverse/brake the spin and orient the feet downward. Release to spin freely." Implement hold: angular velocity strongly damped (e.g. lerp toward small negative) and mild uprighting torque toward feet-down. Release: spin clockwise at base rate * spin stat.

- Kick start: big mechanical foot from top of screen kicks robot after countdown. Nice animation.

- AI: 1-3 opponents racing same course, drawn as full robots in different colors, they never fall apart. Simulate simplified: they move along terrain with bounce, using AI landing quality pseudo-random high. They appear as robots slightly ahead/behind. Need to show position. Keep them on separate lanes? Side view downhill track — use slight y offsets and different x. They should be actual moving entities with bouncing. They progress at target speeds based on level difficulty. Player can beat them.

- Chips: 4 per race: finish 1st, spins challenge (e.g. 3 spins in single jump), jump height (e.g. 18m), distance (e.g. 300m). Awarded on completion; store claimed chip flags per level. Upgrade screen: 4 stats, each up to 8 levels, cost increases. Save to localStorage. Chips as currency plus level chips. "After every race award up to 4 chips" and spend chips on upgrades. Need farm missing chips by replay.

- Tournament: 25-30 levels. Prompt asks at least 8-10 hand-crafted levels. I'll create 30 levels with hand-tuned params and names/themes; distinct configs. "hand-crafted" — define config per level: length, slope, bumpiness, gaps, gravity/planet theme, opponents, chip targets. Procedural terrain from seeds but params hand-authored per level. That's acceptable.

- Menus: title screen with Tournament, Quick Race, Upgrades, Settings, How to Play. Settings: sound toggle, music toggle, reset progress. Practice: choose unlocked level, vs AI or solo. Local multiplayer pass-and-play: up to 3 humans take turns on a single race, each gets 3 attempts? Simpler: "Pass & Play" mode: players take turns racing the same level, best distance/result wins; show final ranking. Include up to 3 humans. Implement mode where after player 1 finishes (or crashes), pass device.

That's a lot. Need to be practical. Build a solid single-file-ish modular TS project:
- src/main.ts – bootstrap, canvas scaling, input
- src/game.ts – state machine / screens
- src/physics/robot.ts
- src/level.ts – level defs + terrain
- src/render.ts? Probably split into draw modules.
- src/ui.ts – menu screens drawn in DOM overlay? For crisp UI easier with DOM/CSS overlay. The game canvas draws action; menus as DOM with CSS. That gives a polished modern look without canvas UI pain. Use HTML/CSS UI overlay, canvas for gameplay. HUD (distance, chips) as DOM too? HUD in canvas is more authentic; but DOM HUD easier. I'll do canvas for HUD to keep CRT-ish style, DOM for menus.

Actually full canvas menus can look more cohesive with the cartoon mobile aesthetic and chunky fonts. But DOM UI is fine and can look pixel-cute with Google font? No network reliance — bundle a font? Use system fonts plus CSS 3D-ish. Could use "Press Start 2P" from Google Fonts but offline builds may fail. Better embed no external font; use a chunky system font stack like "Trebuchet MS", with bold rounded look. For canvas text, use sans-serif bold with thick stroke. Cute enough.

Maybe use DOM for menus with CSS for polished cards/buttons, and canvas for gameplay + HUD. Use a consistent "chunky" style: border 3px solid #2b1c2e, box-shadow offsets, rounded corners, warm palette.

Audio: WebAudio synthesized SFX + chiptune music loop. Implement Music class with simple sequencer using oscillators; upbeat loop. SFX: kick (noise thud), bounce (boing sine glide), metal hit (square noise), explosion (filtered noise), chip (arpeggio), whoosh. Toggle via settings.

Rendering: canvas 480x720 logical portrait.
Scene composition:
- sky gradient per theme (day, sunset, space/planet)
- parallax hills/planets/stars
- ground terrain filled dark dirt with grass top, chunky outline
- finish banner at level end
- player robot: body capsule/torso, head with big eyes, spring feet, arms; limbs drawn if attached. Rotation transforms. Feet orientation indicated.
- AI opponents as smaller robots ahead with different colors.
- particles.
- screen shake on impacts.

Physics detail:
Coordinate system: world x increases right, y increases downward (canvas). Robot pos (x,y), vel (vx,vy). Terrain height function y = groundY(x). Since downhill, groundY increases as x increases? The camera follows; screen position = x - cameraX. Ground descending visually means y grows with x. Terrain starts high on left (y small) and ends low (y large). Robot descends to the right.

But bouncing downhill with bounces: each bounce jumps up (vy negative) and forward (vx positive). We need bounces to feel good, air time long enough to spin.

Gravity ~ 1200 px/s². Robot radius ~ 18 px. Speeds ~ 250-450 px/s. Air time for bounce vy=-450 → ~0.75s → spin 1 rotation maybe at 6 rad/s (0.85 rev/s) → good.

Hmm, easier: world units are meters; scale rendering 5 px/m. Terrain amplitude ~ 15m. Robot radius 2m? Simpler to keep physics in pixels and convert distance to meters via /8.

Let's define world in pixels with 1 unit=px; distance shown = (x - startX)/10 meters. Level length in px: 4800 to 24000. That is fine. Camera 480 wide. Finish line at level.length px. Chips like "distance >= 250m".

Terrain function: use control points at intervals (40-80px) with height. Generate from level params: drop per 1000px = slope; bumps via sum of sine? Need jagged/bumpy look and actual collision. Use piecewise linear segments between control points; raw heightfield array sampled every 16px. Add gaps: regions where ground absent → robot falls into gap; if falls below ground+some threshold, damage and respawn? Original has gaps? Prompt mentions gaps in tournament. Handle gaps as pits: if x inside gap and robot y > groundY + 100 → fall damage + reposition to edge (bad landing), or lose if head. Simpler: gaps cause robot to fall a bit then auto-bounce out with damage (like hitting bottom) — could be jarring. for x from 0 to length step 48:

Need start plateau where robot is perched, then steep drop. Make start at some elevated point; camera initially show cliff top. Level design: first 400px plateau at high y? Actually perch at top of jagged downhill slope: start x=200, ground at y ~ 200; then slope descends. Camera follows.

Jagged bumps: heights vary but keep roughly monotonic downhill. Landing quality affected by slope steepness? Not needed.

Collision: When robot falling (vy>0) and its bottom (pos.y + radius) crosses terrain height at x, then land. Compute height = groundTopAt(x). Robot's contact point at bottom. Set pos.y = height - radius. Compute impact. Also handle being beneath terrain while moving horizontally (upslope) — simple penetration resolution.

Landing resolution:
- angle normalized to [-π, π]; feet-down direction is angle=0 (robot's feet point down when rotation 0). Actually robot sprite drawn with head up, feet at bottom. Rotation 0 = upright.
- feetScore = cos(angle) maybe multiply by facing; use abs for both feet? On both feet means angle near 0. One foot near ±30°.
- angleOff = smallest abs angle to 0 in [0, π].

- perfect: vy = -(baseJump * jumpStat * (1+spinCharge*0.10)) ; vx += 40; damage 0.
- one foot: vy = -(baseJump*0.7*...); damage maybe 0 if stamina high? Prompt: "Landing cleanly on both feet = strong upward/forward bounce and minimal damage." Design damage: Robot has integrity 100 max, affected by stamina stat. Damage amounts: perfect 0, one foot 8, body 16, head 26. Stamina upgrades increase max integrity (100 → 160). When a limb is lost, integrity doesn't reset. Limb removal thresholds: when integrity fraction crosses 80% → right arm, 60% → left arm, 40% → right leg, 20% → left leg. Head eject at <=0 integrity on next bad landing: head launches. This is deterministic and readable. Also spin-charge increases damage risk? Bendy.

Actually "Limbs detach progressively: arms first, then legs" and "When only torso + head remain, next impact can eject head". So track order and thresholds. Integrities at 75, 55, 35, 15 remove arms/legs. At integrity <=0 (next bad impact) head ejects. Head flight = one more chance.

But bad landings reduce bounce, so if you keep failing you slow and lose. To make race finish possible even after head eject: head could be launched forward with high velocity, maybe crosses finish. If head doesn't cross finish and slows to a stop or falls into gap for more than e.g. 2s, race lost (explosion). If it crosses finish, win (still maybe 4th?). Position affects 1st chip only.

# Kamikaze Robots

A complete browser-playable recreation inspired by Digital Chocolate's 2007 Java ME robot racer. Built with HTML5 Canvas, TypeScript and Vite. The art is original vector-style canvas work; no original game assets are required.

## Run it

- **Quick start:** run `./start.sh` in the provided OMGithub environment. The preview server builds and serves the game.
- **Local development:** install Node.js 20+ and run `npm install`, then `npm run dev`. Open the URL Vite prints (usually `http://localhost:5173`).
- **Production build:** `npm run build`; serve the generated `dist/` folder from any static web server.
- **Type check:** `npm run typecheck`.

## Controls

- Hold **Space**, **Down**, **Z**, or press and hold the large on-screen button to brake/reverse your rotation and point the robot's feet down.
- Let go to free-spin clockwise. More spin earns a stronger bounce. Time your brake before you hit the ground.
- **Escape** pauses a race; click the on-screen buttons to resume or quit. **S** opens settings from the main menu.
- Mouse and touch are supported. Sound effects are synthesized locally with Web Audio and can be toggled in-race or in settings.

## Features

- Tournament progression with **30 named, increasingly long and demanding courses**, unlockable in order, and cleared-course replay for chip farming.
- Quick Race / Practice with solo play or up to three configurable AI bots.
- Automatic downhill motion, bump and gap terrain, clockwork kick intro, continuous camera follow, airborne spin control, angle-sensitive landings and springy bounce.
- Progressive damage: arms break first, then legs. If the robot's torso is all that's left, an impact ejects a rocket-powered head that can still cross the finish line.
- Four race objectives (win, spin, height and distance), up to four chips per race, four purchasable upgrades with visible stat effects, and local save data.
- Original cartoon robot/terrain illustration, themed hills and space courses, sparks, debris, screen shake, chiptune-style synthesized SFX, HUD, pause, how-to screen and responsive portrait layout.

## Tuning

- `src/game.ts`: the `LEVELS` list-generation table, `THEMES`, `ground`, physics (`startJump`, `updateActor`, `badImpact`) and rendering.
- `src/main.ts`: menus, controls, race HUD, objective thresholds, progression and upgrades.
- `src/style.css`: interface and responsive styling.

Progress is stored in browser `localStorage` under `kamikaze-save`. Clear the site's storage to reset the tournament.

- Use original vector-style art rather than original game assets.
- Implement 30 increasingly demanding courses, localStorage progression, and keyboard, mouse, and touch controls.
